note: The main banks: Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit and Banco BPM, Italy's three largest banking groups. Intesa Sanpaolo's three personal credit cards, each read on 2026-10-30 from its information sheet: the XME Credit Card (sheet 361, updated 28 October 2026; 5 euros a month), the XME Credit Icon (sheet 362, the same day; 7.50 euros a month) and the Carta di credito Exclusive (sheet 801, updated 23 July 2026; 58 euros a month). Each is a charge card (carta a saldo): the month's spending is taken from the current account in one sum on the 15th of the next month, so nothing is carried. A cash advance costs 4% with a floor of 2.50 euros (Exclusive nothing), and a payment in another currency 2% with a floor of 0.50 euros (Exclusive nothing), the share written as the foreign fee, the floor not modelled. The earlier reading of the XME Credit Card (its account sheet and leaflet, 2026-10-29) holds and is kept as a source. UniCredit's site, its transparency portal (trasparenza.unicredit.it) and its Buddy product sheets all answered 'Request Rejected' (a web application firewall, not circumvented), so no UniCredit card is written. Banco BPM's personal credit cards are issued by Nexi Payments; Nexi's information sheet for cards applied for directly by former Banco BPM customers (no. 1, August 2026) gives the most each card's yearly fee can be, written at that figure: the Carta Nexi (Classic, Choice, FreeTouch and other individual cards) 50 euros, Nexi Prestige 150, Nexi Excellence 300. The cards written are the charge (a saldo) versions; the revolving and optional-instalment versions' rates are set in each holder's SECCI and aren't published in the sheet, and the 'Carte Finanziamento' (35 euros) aren't written for the same reason. A cash advance costs at most 4%, with a floor of 0.52 euros in the euro area (5.16 outside it; the euro-area floor written); a payment in another currency 2.5%; there's no late-payment charge and no default interest. Banco BPM's own transparency page carries a reCAPTCHA and wasn't used. Poste Italiane's card sheets found (the BancoPosta Più revolving card's, May 2018; the corporate card's, 2016) and BNL's TopCredit sheet (November 2010) are too old to stand as current terms and aren't written.
